hugetlb: introduce nr_overcommit_hugepages sysctl
While examining the code to support /proc/sys/vm/hugetlb_dynamic_pool
became convinced that having a boolean sysctl was insufficient:
1) To support per-node control of hugepages
patches to add a sysfs attribute related to nr_hugepages. However
a boolean global value and per-mount quota enforcement constraining the
dynamic pool
column2: adding corresponding control of the dynamic pool on a

column1: per-node basis seems inconsistent to me.
2) Administration of the hugetlb dynamic pool with multiple hugetlbfs
mount points is
column3: more arduous than it needs to be. Each quota

column1: would need to be set separately
column2: and the sum would need to be monitored.

column1: To ease the administration
column2: and to help make the way for per-node

column1: control of the static & dynamic hugepage pool
sysctl
column2: nr_overcommit_hugepages. This value serves as a high watermark

column1: for the overall hugepage pool
column2: while nr_hugepages serves as a low

column1: watermark. The boolean sysctl can then be removed
nr_overcommit_hugepages > 0
indicates the same administrative setting as
hugetlb_dynamic_pool == 1
Quotas still serve as local enforcement of the size of the pool on a
per-mount basis.
A few caveats:
1) There is a race whereby the global surplus huge page counter is
incremented before a hugepage has allocated. Another process could then
try grow the pool
column2: and fail to convert a surplus huge page to a normal

column1: huge page and instead allocate a fresh huge page. I believe this is
benign
column2: as no memory is leaked (the actual pages are still tracked

column1: correctly) and the counters won't go out of sync.
2) Shrinking the static pool while a surplus is in effect will allow the
number of surplus huge pages to exceed the overcommit value. As long as
this condition holds
column3: no more surplus huge pages will be

column1: allowed on the system until one of the two sysctls are increased
sufficiently
column2: or the surplus huge pages go out of use and are freed.

column1: Successfully tested on x86_64 with the current libhugetlbfs snapshot
modified to use the new sysctl.
